Summarise an HMM-SSF fit

Source: R/assessment.R, R/fit.R, R/summary.R
summary.ssf_fit.Rd

For a guided fit, the summary lists the candidates that were tried and gives the ecological labels of the selected fit. A fit from fit_ssf() uses its numerical state names. The state table counts Viterbi assignments. Kernel means and signed directional persistence are included when the movement terms and their density convention are available.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'guided_ssf'
print(
  x,
  digits = 3L,
  assessment = NULL,
  term_labels = NULL,
  step_scale = 1,
  step_unit = "input units",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'ssf_fit'
print(
  x,
  digits = 3L,
  assessment = NULL,
  term_labels = NULL,
  step_scale = 1,
  step_unit = "input units",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'ssf_fit'
summary(
  object,
  assessment = NULL,
  term_labels = NULL,
  step_scale = 1,
  step_unit = "input units",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'guided_ssf'
summary(
  object,
  assessment = NULL,
  term_labels = NULL,
  step_scale = 1,
  step_unit = "input units",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'summary_ssf_fit'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_guided_ssf'
print(x, digits = 4L, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted object or a summary returned by one of these methods.

digits

Number of significant digits to display.

assessment

Optional accepted assessment of the same fit, used for ecological state labels.

term_labels

Optional named character vector of readable names for additional covariates, including reference categories when known. Factor coding is not reconstructed from the coefficient names.

step_scale

Positive multiplier for displayed mean step lengths.

step_unit

Distance unit after applying step_scale. Units are not inferred.

...

Reserved for the generic.

object

An object from fit_ssf() or fit_guided_ssf().

Value

A list with a state table (states), step-selection estimates and standard errors (coefficients), additional covariate effects with conditional 95% Wald intervals (ssf_effects), transition probabilities (transition) and optimisation diagnostics. Kernel means are in the chosen step-length units and describe the baseline kernel when there are lag or hourly effects. Standard errors are available when the fit has a covariance matrix. Daily transition arrays retain the hour dimension. Guided summaries also contain status, taxonomy and candidates. The candidate table gives each code, its outcome and a description of its states when available. When no candidate is selected, only these three components are returned.
